accuracySource: the ablation's own per-capability four-repetition mean, one statistic on all three sides

within.note: Both arms live inside `44835820692`, on the same windows, the same reader and the same 121 questions, so this pair prices the run and not the change: the reference pipeline never reads this arm's ask. It is here because it is the only comparison with no second variable in it.

crossRun.note: The feature arm against the previous dispatch's feature arm. Two variables moved and only one of them was the intended one: the ask (`verbatim-acts` -> `aggregation`) and the multi-session room (`62,000` -> `48,460`). The raw difference is therefore an upper bound on what the ask cost, not a single-variable delta.

doubleDifference.note: The reference-pipeline anchor inside each of the same two runs, differenced the same way: `104.25 -> 101.75` is `-2.50` questions of run-to-run movement on an arm nobody changed. Subtracting that drift from the `-6.25` above leaves `-3.75` questions, which is this row's reading. The room moved the other way by `-22%` characters and section 14.97.5 measured that slope at `+0.25` questions per `+28%`, so the room accounts for about `-0.2` of the `-3.75` and cannot explain it.

reading.preregistered: multi-session correct answers gained >= 9 (S8 row); the plan added that a net gain below +1 question means the ask is void on this arm and the route returns to `verbatim-acts`
reading.measured: minus 3.75 questions: 95.25 against 101.5 on four-repetition means, with the anchor's own drift removed
reading.why: The reference pipeline's aggregation contract, migrated whole onto the multi-session route, costs questions rather than gaining them. The pre-registered anti-criterion fired at the first reading, so the ask returns to `verbatim-acts` and the registered arm does not change.
reading.whatItDoesNotSay: It does not say the reference pipeline's contract is worse than ours. That arm still reads 84.09% on the same 121 questions inside this very artifact, 5.37 points above the treatment, with a smaller window and a reader this arm also uses. The contract works where the evidence is chosen by the pipeline that writes it, and fails when it is laid over a window filled by relevance ranking. The interaction is the finding: an instruction and the selection that feeds it are one mechanism, and a contract cannot be transplanted without the selection that produced it.

failureTaxonomy.note: first repetition, 27 of 121 wrong. Under `verbatim-acts` the same population read 14 numeric mismatches, 2 abstentions and 3 other, so the contract did not move failures out of arithmetic: it added thirteen of them.

goldRanks.note: Read on the fixed order -- this run's `ref` carries the section 145.2 repair -- every gold turn was surfaced and none read `-1`. The window did not starve the reader; the instruction changed what the reader did with the evidence it already had.

note: Written from `tools/readout-arm-run.py` over the downloaded artifact of `44835820692` and, for the anchor drift, over `44829684980`'s artifact read the same way. The row had been `unrun` since it was registered because it named `silent-ask.json#delta.multiSession`, a file that does not exist in this repository; `silent` is also the wrong ask, since it removes the written list (`-26`) rather than migrating the reference's contract.
